title: Rounding to the instruction: decimal places, whole numbers, rounding up ampoules
blurb: Round only the final answer, half-up, to exactly the places the stem asks for, and round ampoules up.
question: Prescription: 1000 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride over 7 hours. "Give your answer to the nearest whole number." What rate is typed?

teach.h: Round once, at the end, as instructed
teach.body: Rule: keep the full calculator value through every step and round only the final answer, to exactly the places the stem asks for. Use conventional half-up rounding: look at the next digit; 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less leaves the digit as it is. Ampoules and vials are rounded UP to the next whole one, because you cannot open part of an ampoule. On the practice test, 166.67 to the nearest whole number was marked correct as 167.
teach.cite: FACTS.md section 5; Pearson practice test (adult paper 1)

steps.label: Full value
steps.sub: Keep every digit on the calculator

teach.body: Ben, 54, on a medical ward, is prescribed 1000 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride over 7 hours; "give your answer to the nearest whole number". 1000 ÷ 7 = 142.857… The digit after the units is 8, so round up: 143 mL per hour. Sense-check: 7 × 143 = 1001, just over 1000.

teach.h: Round at the end vs mid-calculation

teach.text: Rounding mid-calculation: rounding a fraction, a dose or a time before the last step shifts the final digit (3.55 instead of 3.54). Keep the full value on the calculator, or write down every digit on the note board, and round once.

teach.body: "Two decimal places" means two digits after the point: 0.63, not 0.6 or 0.625. "Nearest whole number" means no decimal point at all: 143, not 142.9. Truncating (just chopping digits off) is not rounding: 142.857 chopped is 142, which is wrong.

items: Keep full values; round only the final answer.
Type exactly the instructed decimal places.
Ampoules and vials: round up to whole ones.
Classic errors: rounding mid-way and truncating.

summary: You can now round a final answer half-up to a whole number, one or two decimal places exactly as instructed, and round ampoules up. You can also avoid rounding mid-calculation and truncating.

A.q: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 1000 mL, IV, over 9 hours. At what rate should the infusion pump be set? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

whyNot.0: Rounded up although the next digit (1) is below 5.
whyNot.2: Gave one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.

A.q: You have a prescription for 50 mg. The ampoule label reads 30 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: Truncated 1.666...; the next digit is 6, so round up.
whyNot.1: Gave two decimal places; the stem asks for one.

A.q: You have a prescription for 300 micrograms of a medicine. It is supplied in ampoules of 250 micrograms. How many ampoules need to be opened?

whyNot.1: Rounded down: 1 ampoule holds only 250 micrograms.
whyNot.2: You cannot open part of an ampoule.
whyNot.3: Rounded up by more than needed.

B.q: You have a prescription for 45 mg. The ampoule label reads 80 mg in 2 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.
B.why: 45 ÷ 80 × 2 = 1.125. The third digit is 5, so round up: 1.13 mL.

whyNot.0: Rounded the final 5 down; half-up rounding gives 1.13.
whyNot.1: Gave one decimal place; the stem asks for two.

B.q: Prescription: Hartmann's solution, 500 mL, IV, over 2 hours 40 minutes. At what rate should the infusion pump be set? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
B.why: 2 hours 40 minutes = 2.666... hours. 500 ÷ 2.666... = 187.5, so 188 mL per hour.

whyNot.1: Rounded the time to 2.6 hours before dividing.
whyNot.2: Rounded the time to 2.7 hours before dividing.

B.q: A person weighing 63 kg is prescribed 0.15 mg/kg of a medicine. The ampoule label reads 4 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.0: Rounded the dose (9.45 mg) to 9.5 mg before dividing.
whyNot.2: Gave one decimal place; the stem asks for two.

C.q: Prescription: 5% glucose, 1000 mL, IV, over 6 hours 30 minutes. At what rate should the infusion pump be set? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
C.why: 6 hours 30 minutes = 6.5 hours. 1000 ÷ 6.5 = 153.84..., so 154 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: Truncated 153.8...; the next digit is 8, so round up.
whyNot.2: Rounded the time down to 6 hours first.

C.q: A person is prescribed 1.2 mg of a medicine three times a day. Each dose is drawn from new 1 mg ampoules and any remainder is discarded. How many ampoules are needed in 24 hours?
C.why: Each dose: 1.2 ÷ 1 = 1.2, rounded up to 2 ampoules. Three doses: 3 × 2 = 6 ampoules.

whyNot.0: Rounded the daily total (3.6 mg) up; each dose needs its own 2 ampoules.
whyNot.2: Rounded each dose down to 1 ampoule.
whyNot.3: Ampoules are whole; this is the dose in mg.

C.q: A child is prescribed 37 mg of a medicine. The bottle label reads 120 mg/5 mL. What volume should be given? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.1: Gave one decimal place; the stem asks for two.

reteach.title: Full value, one rounding
reteach.question: 1000 mL over 7 hours, nearest whole number: what is typed?

blocks.h: Look one place to the right
blocks.body: 1000 ÷ 7 = 142.857… The whole-number place is the 2; the next digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so the 2 becomes 3: 143.

blocks.text: Chopping off the decimals gives 142: that is truncating, not rounding.

explain.body: If the next digit is 5 or more, round up; if 4 or less, leave it.

test.q: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 1000 mL, IV, over 7 hours. At what rate should the infusion pump be set? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

whyNot.1: Gave two decimal places; the stem asks for a whole number.

explain.body: One decimal place means one digit after the point.

test.q: You have a prescription for 37 mg. The ampoule label reads 15 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

explain.body: Any part of an ampoule means opening a whole one.

test.q: You have a prescription for 1.5 mg of a medicine. It is supplied in 1 mg ampoules. How many ampoules need to be opened?

whyNot.0: Rounded down; 1 ampoule holds only 1 mg.
whyNot.2: You cannot open half an ampoule.

explain.body: Keep 65 ÷ 120 as 0.541666… and multiply before rounding.

test.q: You have a prescription for 65 mg. The bottle label reads 120 mg/5 mL. What volume should be given? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.
